keyVerseText: But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.
rootMeaning: The Greek verb διαδίδωμι (diadídōmi) originates from the preposition διά (diá), meaning 'through' or 'by means of,' combined with δίδωμι, meaning 'to give.' Thus, its root sense conveys the act of giving or handing over something through or among a group, emphasizing distribution or transmission across a space or to multiple recipients. This etymology enriches the English glosses like 'distribute' or 'divide' by highlighting the movement and spreading out inherent in the action, rather than a simple one-to-one giving.
usageInScripture: In Scripture, διαδίδωμι appears in five occurrences, where it is translated variously as 'divideth,' 'distribute,' 'he distributed,' 'distribution was made,' and 'shall give.' This range of translations reflects the word's core meaning of handing over or spreading out, whether referring to dividing spoils, distributing food, or delivering something to others. The consistency of these uses underscores the word's emphasis on allocation and transmission, whether physically or figuratively.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding διαδίδωμι deepens our grasp of how God’s blessings, authority, and truth are given and shared within the community of faith. The concept of handing over or distributing speaks to the stewardship entrusted to believers to share spiritual gifts, truths, and resources with others. It also reminds us of Christ’s victory, who overcomes and takes spoils, distributing them according to divine purpose. This word highlights the dynamic and communal nature of God’s work—His grace is not hoarded but given out abundantly and passed on through successive generations and believers.
keyVerseReflection: Luke 11:22 states, 'But when a stronger than he shall come upon him, and overcome him, he taketh from him all his armour wherein he trusted, and divideth his spoils.' Here, διαδίδωμι vividly portrays the victorious act of dividing or distributing spoils after overcoming an adversary. The use of this word emphasizes not only the defeat of the enemy but also the rightful allocation of what was taken, illustrating Christ’s supreme authority to claim and distribute victory and blessings. It highlights the transfer of power and resources from the defeated to the conqueror.
